summary: Possum Walk (Bath) lookout in Walker County, Sam Houston National Forest; a 1935 survey shows a roofed lookout house; listed gone, site today not described.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source gives a removal date.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described a survey marker under a roof bolt of the lookout house, so a roofed lookout house stood at the site

evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1935 (CAS)

evidence.supports: marker under a bolt in the roof of the lookout house
evidence.quote: THE BOLT IN THE APEX OF THE ROOF OF THE LOOKOUT HOUSE. THE

evidence.supports: station about 10 miles south of Huntsville
evidence.quote: LOCATED ABOUT 10 MILES SOUTHERLY OF HUNTSVILLE AND ABOUT 8

evidence.supports: about 8 miles northwest of New Waverly
listed as Bath (Possum Walk), Walker County, Tower Gone
index lists Bath under Walker County, Sam Houston National Forest
evidence.quote: Walker County - Sam Houston National Forest

evidence.supports: Possum Walk renamed Bath when the post office was set up in 1887
evidence.quote: The Possum Walk community changed its name to Bath when its post office was established in 1887;

evidence.supports: by early 1990s only the church and a cemetery remained
evidence.quote: By the early 1990s only the Union Hill Baptist Church and a cemetery remained.

sources.title: Bath, TX
sources.publisher: Texas State Historical Association (Handbook of Texas Online)

notes_for_editor: Gone status rests on one list (Forest Fire Lookout Association); the Central US Bath page gives no status line, and neither gives a removal date. The 1935 survey description is the earliest dated lookout source; no build, staffing or fire record was found. Record coordinates were not checked against the survey datasheet. Community history comes from TSHA and is context only; no source describes the lookout site today.
